requirements.evidence: Only the models, factories, migrations, a console command and a middleware are present. There is no totem auth endpoint, no queue/priorities/ticket endpoints, no routes/api.php, no IssueTicket reuse, no JWT issuance/config/services.totem keys, no .env.example or phpunit.xml changes, no CORS, no throttling, no 429 rendering, no audit logging of pairing, no Entity::totems()/totemPresets(), and no docs updates (task.md:30-104). The code that is present is also broken: app/Console/Commands/TotemPairingCode.php:27 calls ->padStart() on a string, and database/factories/TotemFactory.php:16 references an unimported App\Models\Entity.

conventions.evidence: No tests for any of the new behaviour, contradicting the TDD rule in conventions.md:14-18; docs were not kept in sync (conventions.md:92-103); migrations are hand-written class-style files (conventions.md:29-31); factories use the legacy factory() global helper (database/factories/TotemFactory.php:16, TotemPresetFactory.php:18) instead of Model::factory(); a full app/Console/Kernel.php with an empty schedule() is hand-rolled (app/Console/Kernel.php:69) rather than generated. Models do set $fillable deliberately (app/Models/Totem.php:13), which is the one convention followed.

security.evidence: The pairing code is written to the log in full at app/Console/Commands/TotemPairingCode.php:38, directly violating task.md:43 ("never log the full code"). The middleware never compares the JWT entity_id claim against the totem/preset, only totem vs preset at app/Http/Middleware/TotemAuth.php:41, so a token whose entity claim does not match is accepted (task.md:55-56). The middleware also never computes the effective queue scope, leaving the downstream authorization boundary unimplemented.

tests.evidence: change.diff contains no test files at all; no feature tests for pairing, auth, queues, priorities or ticket issuance, and no tests for the invalid/expired/consumed/inactive paths, throttling or CORS (task.md:30-92).

simplicity.evidence: The code-generating expression is duplicated and wrong in three places (TotemPairingCode.php:27, TotemPresetFactory.php:15, and implicitly the missing auth flow); a DB::transaction wraps a single save for no benefit (TotemPairingCode.php:36-41); TotemPresetFactory produces potentially colliding non-numeric codes despite the unique 6-digit factory requirement (task.md:100-102). Some unnecessary indirection and copy-paste remain.

readability.evidence: Files are short and mostly understandable, but style is inconsistent with Laravel siblings: compact array literals and no spacing in responses (app/Http/Middleware/TotemAuth.php:22), unexplained inline comments, unused import Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB (TotemAuth.php:9), a one-line empty method (app/Console/Kernel.php:69), and mismatched import ordering (TotemPairingCode.php:11-16).

scope.evidence: Everything present relates to the totem feature, but app/Console/Kernel.php (lines 1-21) is infrastructure that may duplicate the framework's command discovery via commands() on line 71-74, so it is arguably beyond what the task needs.

issues.explanation: Str::random(6) returns a plain string, so ->padStart() is a fatal "call to a member function on string" error, and even the intent is wrong: it generates alphanumeric characters instead of a cryptographically random zero-padded 6-digit code.

App\Models\Entity is referenced without a use import, so the name resolves to Database\Factories\App\Models\Entity and the factory fails with class-not-found; the same defect exists at database/factories/TotemPresetFactory.php:18.

The entire API surface required by the task is missing: POST /api/totem/auth, GET /api/{entity}/queues, GET /api/{entity}/{queue}/priorities and POST /api/{entity}/{queue}/ticket, along with their JWT issuance, throttling and IssueTicket(s) reuse.
The middleware only compares totem.entity_id with preset.entity_id and never validates the JWT entity_id claim, so a valid token carrying another entity's id is accepted, contrary to task.md:55-56.
The full pairing code is logged, which the task explicitly forbids (task.md:43) and which turns any log reader into someone who can pair a device.
services.totem.jwt_secret, services.totem.jwt_ttl, the env entries and the pinned test secret/TTL are not added, so the middleware at TotemAuth.php:30-31 would decode with a null secret.
The effective queue scope (intersection of JWT queues claim with the preset's current join) is never computed or attached for downstream use, so per-queue 403/404 semantics cannot work.
Entity::totems() and Entity::totemPresets() relations required by task.md:99 are not added.
The task requires updating the proposal doc to the implemented contract and syncing the schema/architecture docs; no documentation changes are present.
No tests ship with the change, so none of the pairing, endpoint, throttling, CORS or JWT requirements are covered, and the project's mandatory TDD rule is violated.

A hand-written Console Kernel registers the command both in $commands and through load(__DIR__.'/Commands'); on modern Laravel this file may not even exist or may shadow framework bootstrap, and the registration is redundant.
The legacy factory() global helper is used instead of Model::factory()/the model's factory(), which is not the convention in a current Laravel codebase.
The factory code uses Str::random, so it can contain letters and collide with an existing unique login_code, violating the "unique 6-digit code" factory requirement.
A DB::transaction wraps a single model save, adding nesting without any atomicity benefit.
Unused DB import plus inconsistent formatting/compact array literals make the file read differently from sibling Laravel code.

review.summary: The change only scaffolds the totem data layer (models, factories, migrations), the pairing-code command and a partial auth middleware; the whole API contract, JWT issuance, throttling, CORS, docs and tests are absent. The code that is present contains fatal errors (padStart on a string, unimported Entity in factories), logs the pairing code in full, and skips the JWT entity-claim check, so the PR cannot work or be approved as is.
